subject: interactive accessibility behavior

cases.scenario: A custom modal opens from a button. Keyboard users cannot Escape to close it, tab focus escapes behind the overlay, and focus is lost after close.
cases.context: The modal is implemented in React with divs and custom click handlers.
cases.question: What accessibility fixes should be required?
expected_flags: Keyboard operation and focus management are core accessibility behavior.
Focus should move into the modal on open, stay contained while open, and return to the trigger on close.
Escape close behavior and visible focus must be tested.
expected_fix_hints: Use an accessible dialog pattern or native primitives where available.
Wire Escape, tab containment, aria-modal/dialog labelling, and focus return.
Verify with keyboard-only navigation and assistive technology announcements.
absent_signals: Do not treat this as visual polish.
Do not add ARIA without matching keyboard behavior.

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Keyboard operation and focus management are core accessibility behavior.
Surfaces this expected flag: Focus should move into the modal on open, stay contained while open, and return to the trigger on close.
Surfaces this expected flag: Escape close behavior and visible focus must be tested.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Use an accessible dialog pattern or native primitives where available.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Wire Escape, tab containment, aria-modal/dialog labelling, and focus return.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Verify with keyboard-only navigation and assistive technology announcements.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not treat this as visual polish.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not add ARIA without matching keyboard behavior.

cases.scenario: A form shows validation errors visually after submit, but screen reader users do not hear that the state changed.
cases.context: Inputs have visible text labels, but errors are rendered in a toast at the bottom of the page.
cases.question: How should the implementation change?
expected_flags: Validation state changes must be perceivable to assistive technology.
Errors need programmatic association with their fields or a live region summary.
expected_fix_hints: Use aria-describedby or equivalent field-error association.
Add a role=status or role=alert/live region for summary changes when appropriate.
Keep labels and error text programmatically reachable.
absent_signals: Do not only rewrite the text tone.
Do not rely on color or toast placement as the accessibility fix.

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Validation state changes must be perceivable to assistive technology.
Surfaces this expected flag: Errors need programmatic association with their fields or a live region summary.
Surfaces this expected flag: Visible-only toast feedback is insufficient.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Use aria-describedby or equivalent field-error association.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Add a role=status or role=alert/live region for summary changes when appropriate.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Keep labels and error text programmatically reachable.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not only rewrite the text tone.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not rely on color or toast placement as the accessibility fix.

cases.scenario: A user says: 'Rewrite this error message at a sixth-grade reading level.'
cases.context: No interactive behavior, semantic HTML, keyboard flow, focus management, or assistive-technology announcement issue is present.
cases.question: Should a11y own this request?
expected_flags: This is language/readability work, not interactive accessibility implementation.
The correct owner is linguistics, documentation, or microcopy depending on context.
a11y should not over-trigger on every use of the word accessible.
expected_fix_hints: Only re-enter a11y if the message has programmatic labeling, announcement, or interaction implications.
absent_signals: Do not claim reading level alone proves accessibility compliance.
Do not prescribe ARIA for a pure copy rewrite.

cases.scenario: A custom account menu opens on click, but arrow keys do nothing, Escape does not close the menu, and focus remains on a hidden item after the menu closes.
cases.context: The component is implemented with div elements and click handlers in a React navigation bar.
cases.question: What should be required before this menu ships?
expected_flags: Keyboard behavior is a core accessibility requirement for custom interactive widgets.
The menu needs a coherent focus model while open and after close.
ARIA role/name/state must match the actual keyboard behavior.
expected_fix_hints: Prefer a native or proven accessible menu/disclosure pattern when possible.
Implement and test arrow-key or disclosure-appropriate keyboard behavior, Escape close, visible focus, and focus return.
Expose programmatic names and expanded/open state that match the visible UI.
absent_signals: Do not add ARIA roles without implementing the required keyboard behavior.

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Keyboard behavior is a core accessibility requirement for custom interactive widgets.
Surfaces this expected flag: The menu needs a coherent focus model while open and after close.
Surfaces this expected flag: ARIA role/name/state must match the actual keyboard behavior.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Prefer a native or proven accessible menu/disclosure pattern when possible.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Implement and test arrow-key or disclosure-appropriate keyboard behavior, Escape close, visible focus, and focus return.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Expose programmatic names and expanded/open state that match the visible UI.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not approve click-only interaction.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not add ARIA roles without implementing the required keyboard behavior.

cases.scenario: A user asks for a more premium visual style for a button: different radius, shadow, and brand color. No contrast, keyboard, focus, semantic, labeling, or state-announcement problem is described.
cases.context: The button is already a native button with a visible focus indicator and accessible name.
cases.question: Should a11y own this request?
expected_flags: This is visual design work unless the requested color or styling harms perceivability.
The correct owner is visual-design-foundations or color-system-design for brand styling.
a11y re-enters scope only when contrast, focus visibility, semantics, keyboard operation, naming, or announcements are affected.
expected_fix_hints: Route the visual-branding request to the design skill.
Keep an accessibility check only as a verification constraint for contrast and focus visibility if styling changes.
absent_signals: Do not treat all button styling as a11y-owned implementation work.
Do not prescribe ARIA for a purely visual styling request.
